cards.title: I want to build an audit logging, authentication and authorization…
cards.one_line: I want to build an audit logging, authentication and authorization layer for physical AI agents, like robots and drones that act in the real world. HarnessRouter already puts one API in front of many agent harnesses, which makes it the right place to check every agent’s identity, enforce what it’s allowed to do, and record each decision before it turns into a physical action. This is for robotics teams and companies deploying autonomous machines in places like warehouses, factories and hospitals. They need to prove what their agents did and why, and stop unsafe actions before they happen.

cards.title: An autonomous AI agent powered by HarnessRouter that turns any…
cards.one_line: An autonomous AI agent powered by HarnessRouter that turns any undocumented website, legacy portal, or raw network trace into a tested, production-ready FastAPI microservice in minutes. Instead of forcing engineers to spend days manually inspecting browser traffic, writing brittle scrapers, and debugging pagination or rate limits, users simply input a target URL and a data goal. Inside an isolated sandbox, the agent uses a low-cost harness to filter live DOM and network packets, routes the distilled schema to a high-reasoning coding harness to generate clean Python code and automated pytest checks, and self-heals until every edge case passes. By replacing $5,000+ freelance data-engineering gigs with a $50 automated run that costs pennies in compute, BlackBox API delivers immediate, verifiable ROI for lead-generation agencies, supply chain teams, and AI builders.

cards.title: I'd like to build a fault-tolerant multi-agent system that can detect…
cards.one_line: I'd like to build a fault-tolerant multi-agent system that can detect failures, prevent error propagation, and recover efficiently using dependency-aware recovery rather than restarting entire workflows. I have experience working on this problem through my current research project at UC San Diego, where I've been developing a multi-agent framework to inject faults such as incorrect agent outputs, timeouts, and tool failures, and evaluate how these failures propagate through downstream agents. I've also been exploring recovery strategies that minimize redundant computation while maintaining task success rates. I'd like to use HarnessRouter to extend this work into a practical, reliable AI agent infrastructure solution for AI startups and engineering teams building production-grade agentic applications.

cards.title: An estimate-revival agent for SF remodelers, ADU builders, and general…
cards.one_line: An estimate-revival agent for SF remodelers, ADU builders, and general contractors. These shops send out high-ticket quotes all the time, and a lot of them die because nobody follows up. The agent pulls the contractor’s unsigned past quotes, follows up by text, email, and phone in their voice, handles the replies, and books site visits straight onto their calendar. They pay per booked site visit, so they only pay when it works. I’m already building this as my company, Leek (voice stack on Vapi, Twilio, and Cal.com). I’d use HarnessRouter for the agent layer: reading quotes, writing follow-ups, and handling the back-and-forth. That way I can spend build week getting real contractors live instead of wiring up harnesses.

cards.title: I want to build "Secretly Stanford?", a Big Game week app for Cal and…
cards.one_line: I want to build "Secretly Stanford?", a Big Game week app for Cal and Stanford students that settles the oldest rivalry accusation: upload your class schedule, Spotify top artists and a few camera-roll photos, and it tells you what percent Stanford you really are, with a roast to back it up. Behind the scenes, each person gets a sandboxed HarnessRouter run where an agent analyzes what they shared, writes the verdict and renders a story-sized card they can post in seconds. Because HarnessRouter puts Claude Code, Codex and others behind one API, one harness argues you’re a true Bear while another argues you belong in Palo Alto, and your card shows who won the debate.
